title: token-level observability: cost/latency breakdowns, traces, and alert tuning
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: provide token-level cost and latency observability across the serving runtime to help SREs and product teams identify hot prompts, regression sources, and unit-cost anomalies. This PR adds: 1) token-level metrics (per-request token emit rate, per-token CPU/GPU micro-ops estimate), 2) tracing spans for request->batch->kernel stages, 3) new Grafana dashboards with cost/latency breakdown panels, and 4) tuned alerts for token-level tail latency and cost regressions. Design notes: - Metrics are implemented with controlled cardinality: we only tag token-level metrics with model_family and route, not full prompt hashes, and we sample metadata for high-cardinality traffic. - Traces are correlated via request_id and batch_id; KV-cache hits are annotated to help identify cache-induced latency drops. - Dashboards include a new Cost Attribution panel that combines token counts, model variant pricing profiles, and observed latency to estimate per-route unit economics. Checklist: - [x] Add token-level counters and histograms (server runtime) - [x] Add tracing spans and context propagation (runtime & gateway) - [x] Add Grafana dashboards + JSON model - [x] Add alert rules in prometheus/rules - [x] Add e2e smoke test for telemetry pipeline - [x] Update SLO runbook snippets - [x] Add docs snippet to observability-pack This description includes the motivation, approach, and rollout notes. Rollout plan: feature-gate token-level metrics behind a runtime flag (off by default), enable in staging for 48h, run synthetic prompt sets (ENG-1428) to validate no cardinality explosion, then flip on in production incrementally by customer tier. Related: references pr-20413, pr-19785 for previous dashboard iterations and ENG-1428 for the evaluation harness used to validate cost calculations.

review_conversation: Diego Morales (reviewer): Can we avoid high-cardinality tags by replacing prompt_id with route and model_family? Also request a sampling strategy for high-QPS routes.
Asha Patel (author): Good catch - implemented tag normalization and added a reservoir sampler for routes exceeding a configurable token-per-second threshold. See token_metrics.rs lines 120-190.
Lena Kim (reviewer): The Prometheus alert thresholds look aggressive for small customers. Suggest adding a tiered threshold based on customer_tier label.
Asha Patel (author): Added tiered thresholds and a runbook section describing mitigation steps. Alerts default to SLO-safe thresholds for free-tier and stricter for enterprise-tier.
Samir Rao (reviewer): Traces look good; can you add a dashboard panel that surfaces top-k prompts by estimated unit cost?
Asha Patel (author): Added Cost Attribution top-k panel that uses sampled prompt metadata and per-token pricing profile mapping.
